Miracle on the Mississippi: All accounted for after tanker collides with cruise ship

cards.what_happened: A tanker called Atlantic Asphalt hit the docked river cruise ship American Heritage on the Mississippi River in New Orleans at about 12.30pm on Friday. Rescue crews pulled people from the water as the cruise ship slowly rolled onto its side, and 24 patients were admitted to hospital. The river was closed to all vessel traffic while responders worked.
details: The tanker Atlantic Asphalt collided with American Cruise Lines' American Heritage at about 12.30pm on Friday while it was docked on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, said Kimberly Curth, Port of New Orleans press secretary. The cruise ship had about 129 passengers plus crew onboard and had docked about two hours earlier to begin passenger disembarkation.

New Orleans firefighters, port and city police, the US Coast Guard and emergency medical staff worked to pull people from the water, and mayor Helena Moreno's office said multiple individuals had been rescued. Video showed tugboat crew pulling people in lifejackets or holding flotation rings from the river, and those who got off were brought inside the port's administration building. LCMC, which runs University Medical Center, said 24 patients were admitted, Acadian Ambulance took eight people to hospital with injuries not yet known, and the Coast Guard closed the river to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96.

Video showed the American Heritage slowly roll onto its side, and witness Jamie Holford told WDSU it took 15 minutes from impact to rolling over, calling it surreal. Maritime law expert Martin J Davies of Tulane University told WVUE the tanker was lucky not to strike the Crescent City Connection bridge, which carries about 160,000 cars daily. Officials gave no cause; one emergency source said the tanker may have lost power, unconfirmed, and American Cruise Lines said guests and crew were evacuated without giving numbers.

The American Heritage is a 300ft paddle-wheel ship built in 2015, previously the Queen of the Mississippi, with more than 80 staterooms; the Atlantic Asphalt is an oil tanker built in 2017, about 160 meters long, deadweight 17,764 metric tons, flying the Marshall Islands flag, owned and commercially operated by Nave Shipping SA, a company registered in Liberia, with maintenance, technical and safety work overseen by Singapore-based Thome Ship Management. It is not on international sanctions lists checked by services including Magic Port, but Canadian authorities fined it C$7,800, recorded 11 August 2020, after an officer failed to properly supervise a transfer operation. Rescue activity scaled back later on Friday, and Louisiana governor Jeff Landry said he was headed to New Orleans.
key_facts: Tanker Atlantic Asphalt hit docked cruise ship American Heritage on the Mississippi River in New Orleans Friday about 12.30pm.
About 129 passengers plus crew were aboard; the ship had docked two hours earlier to begin disembarkation.
Guests and crew evacuated; rescuers pulled people from water as the ship slowly rolled onto its side.
LCMC said 24 patients were admitted; Acadian Ambulance took eight people to hospital, injuries not yet known.
Coast Guard closed the river to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96 for response work.
Expert said tanker lucky not to hit bridge carrying about 160,000 cars daily; cause unknown, power loss unconfirmed.
American Heritage: 300ft paddle-wheel ship built 2015; Atlantic Asphalt: oil tanker built 2017, Marshall Islands flag, Nave Shipping SA.
Tanker fined C$7,800 by Canada on 11 August 2020; Governor Jeff Landry said he was headed to New Orleans.
cards.whats_next: The river stays closed to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96 while responders assess the situation, and Louisiana governor Jeff Landry said he was headed to New Orleans.
cards.blurb: A tanker struck a docked Mississippi River cruise ship in New Orleans, rolling it onto its side; 24 patients were admitted.

Exercise book prices to fall by 18% from December 1

cards.what_happened: The National Book Traders' Association announced that retail prices of all exercise books across the island will be reduced by 18% starting December 1. It says the nationwide reduction is a direct result of VAT exemptions and concessions proposed under the 2027 National Budget.
details: The National Book Traders' Association has announced that the retail prices of all exercise books across the island will be reduced by 18% starting December 1. The price reduction applies nationwide.

The association says the nationwide reduction comes as a direct result of the Value Added Tax (VAT) exemptions and concessions proposed under the 2027 National Budget. The announcement was reported by Newswire.
key_facts: National Book Traders' Association announced an 18% cut in retail prices of all exercise books.
The price reduction starts December 1 and applies across the island.
The cut is a direct result of VAT exemptions and concessions.
Those VAT exemptions and concessions are proposed under the 2027 National Budget.
The announcement was reported by Newswire.
cards.whats_next: Exercise book retail prices will be reduced by 18% starting December 1.
cards.blurb: Exercise books will cost 18% less from December 1, after VAT exemptions and concessions in the 2027 National Budget.
cards.spoken: Good evening. If you buy exercise books, there is some news for you. The National Book Traders' Association has announced that the retail prices of all exercise books across the island will be reduced by 18% starting December 1. That is a nationwide price reduction. The association says this cut comes as a direct result of the Value Added Tax, or VAT, exemptions and concessions proposed under the 2027 National Budget. So from December 1, every exercise book sold across the island will carry a price that is 18% lower. That is the announcement from the National Book Traders' Association, reported by Newswire.
